title: Email: Turnaround Cleaning Order and the Shell Door Conflict

fields.to: VP Fleet Operations Colleen Abernathy-Reyes; Hotel Director
fields.subject: Turnaround cleaning order, agreed with the terminal: decision needed by 11:00
fields.body:
Both,

Gulf Terminal Services and I agreed this at 10:35. Here is the order:

(1) CABINS FIRST: all 1,490 cabins at 1,000 ppm. All 380 stewards work in 19 teams of 20, moving forward to aft. Gowned teams do the isolation cabins and companion cabins last. All bedding and soft furnishings go to laundry at 60 C.

(2) PUBLIC AREAS after the cabins: the Lido, dining rooms, show lounge, kids club, elevators and handrails.

(3) TERMINAL LAST: terminal staff clean the check-in hall, seating and restrooms. Our Environmental Officer signs that off.

Conflicts:
- The 12 provisioning trucks need the forward shell door and 60 crew on stores loading from 11:00 to 15:00. The cabin teams use the same corridor for linen carts.
- About 210 crew sign off and 195 sign on through the crew gangway from 11:30. 34 of the crew leaving are stewards.
- Laundry: we expect about 9.5 tons of soft goods, and capacity is 14 tons a day. The last loads won't finish before about 17:30.

By 11:00 I need a yes on this order, and a decision on whether the trucks or the linen carts get the shell door first. The terminal is holding the lane plan until it hears from us.
fields.signature:
Hector Salazar
Port Operations Manager, Galveston
Halcyon Reach Cruises

instructorNote: This inject checks whether OPS and HOTEL make the cleaning order the critical path. Look for OPS approving the order and giving the linen carts the shell door, with provisioning moved to the aft door or later slots, and for HOTEL keeping or replacing the 34 departing stewards and logging the swaps. Both should confirm that the full outbreak clean in HOPRPG 6 and the Environmental Officer's walk-through stay the condition for boarding.
